explanation: The top of a lighthouse is its lantern, and the one who tends it is the keeper. The film's watchman and his grey cat won the Gold Gull a year after its release.

claims.text: Only the answer fits clues 1 to 3.
Its title names the job of whoever tends the lamp at the top of a lighthouse.
Its hero tends a light on a sea rock for thirty winters with a grey cat.
This fixture film won the Gold Gull prize in 1988, the year after it came out.
One word of its title names the glass room that holds a lighthouse's lamp.
Each distractor contradicts at least one of clues 1 to 3.

writerNotes: Invented fixture for tests, the mock backend and the e2e track (ARCHITECTURE 5.6). Not a real fact; never scheduled on the main track. Every film in the list is invented, so the ladder is solved from the titles and years that the suggestions show (R1-30): clue 1 names the title as a job, clue 2 sets the decoys (the films with Lighthouse in the title), and clue 3's year keeps only the 1987 film. Clue 4 is a fact of its own, never clue 2 again: the lantern, the glass room at the top of a lighthouse, which no other option's title names.
